To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
RNA is a modular biomolecule composed of a relatively small number of common structural motifs that are used in a wide variety of RNA molecules.
RNA secondary structure motifs can be classified by their structure and that these motifs are composed of structural elements that can be classified by structure.

RNA is a modular biomolecule, that it is composed largely of conservatively conserved structural sub-units, or motifs, that these structural motifs are to be distinguished by sequence, function or tertiary structure, that a limited number of structural motifs can be identified in hairpin and internal loop sequences and that these structural motifs appear to be composed largely of a limited number (4–6) of structural elements.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterization of structural motifs and their use in the rational design of RNA structures and in the prediction of RNA secondary structure.
the structural motifs that are the fundamental components of RNA structure and function.
the structural, evolutionary, and functional aspects of RNA motifs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
RNA structural motifs are the building blocks of RNA.
the RNA structural motifs are the basic building blocks for RNA folding.
we are at a stage of discovery of RNA structure and function that is analogous to the discovery of protein structure and function in the 1930s and 1940s.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the RNA structural motifs that are known today are the building blocks of a highly complex modular biomolecule.
the RNA motif is a building block of RNA secondary and tertiary structure, and that RNA motifs are a modular component of RNA structure.
RNA structural motifs are a key to understanding the structure and function of RNA and are likely to have an impact on the design of new RNA molecules with novel functions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are only a small number of motifs that are found in a large variety of RNAs.
RNA is a modular biomolecule, composed largely of common structural motifs, which may be used as a scaffold for RNA engineering.

RNA motifs are a useful concept for describing and analyzing RNA structure, and that the modular nature of the RNA structure is an important feature of RNA that is being exploited for RNA design and engineering.
